management_notes: CEO Tasheel Jeerh (effective May 5, 2026) completed delivery on the Spring 2026 commitment: 23 drillholes and 4,267m at Pomley Cove Pond and Frost Cove North, with headline assays released August 29, 2026. The simultaneous launch of the 5,000m Taylor Brook program backed by a closed $2,600,000 placement demonstrates sequential capital market access across multiple NL property targets. Score of 3 is maintained: execution risk on the Spring 2026 program has resolved and capital allocation across multiple fronts is disciplined. Constraining factors remain: insider ownership levels and the CEO's broader track record prior to Churchill are unconfirmable from public sources; management depth below the CEO/IR level is thin for a multi-property district explorer.
geology_notes: Spring 2026 assay results are now public (released August 29, 2026). Headline intercept confirmed: 19.23% Sb over 1.40m at Frost Cove North from a 23-hole, 4,267m program at Pomley Cove Pond and Frost Cove North. A copper-silver discovery returned 0.78% Cu with 6.12 g/t Ag over 6.22m, broadening the polymetallic thesis beyond the core antimony-gold story. Cumulative confirmed highlights across the Black Raven district: (1) 19.23% Sb over 1.40m at Frost Cove North (Spring 2026); (2) 35.1% and 29.7% Sb at Black Raven past-producers; (3) 13.00% Sb over 0.57m at Frost Cove (May 2026); (4) 9.46% Sb with 35.5 g/t Au and 1,118 g/t Ag discovered 1.2km north of the historic mine; (5) 7.25% Sb over 1.98m at a second polymetallic system near the southern shaft; (6) 17.3 g/t Au and 130 g/t Ag at Pomley Cove Pond veins; (7) up to 12.11% Zn grab samples at Black Raven; (8) Taylors Room: 10.59 g/t AuEq over 1.05m and 4.12 g/t AuEq over 1.80m; (9) new Cu-Ag intercept 0.78% Cu / 6.12 g/t Ag over 6.22m. The August 2023 NI 43-101 technical report remains the most recent on file; all resource/reserve fields are null per the extracted filings. The 5,000m Taylor Brook program is now active. Score of 3 is maintained: confirmed high-grade, multi-commodity mineralisation across an expanding NL district, constrained by the absence of a compliant resource estimate and the early stage of Taylor Brook.

catalyst_notes: Spring 2026 assay results released August 29, 2026 — the primary near-term catalyst has now fired and is one day old. Market digestion of the 19.23% Sb / 1.40m headline and new Cu-Ag system (0.78% Cu / 6.12 g/t Ag / 6.22m) is underway. The active 5,000m Taylor Brook drill program represents the next significant catalyst window; first assay results from Taylor Brook are expected in coming months. The new Cu-Ag discovery could generate independent follow-up drilling as a third catalyst stream beyond Taylor Brook and further Black Raven extensions. Macro: China's September 2024 antimony export controls remain in force; US DoD critical minerals grant programs have awarded over USD $100M to Tier-1 jurisdiction antimony projects since late 2025, sustaining strategic buyer attention. Score of 3 is maintained: one catalyst fired (resolved positively), Taylor Brook and Cu-Ag follow-up open fresh catalyst windows; the macro tailwind is durable and the government-buyer thesis remains intact.
acquisition_notes: No NI 43-101 resource estimate on file; nav_per_share is null and a P/NAV acquisition analysis cannot be performed. The Spring 2026 assay release with a 19.23% Sb headline and new Cu-Ag discovery makes prospective acquirer due diligence more tractable than under prior assay silence, and the polymetallic footprint (Sb, Au, Ag, Cu, Zn) provides multiple commodity hooks for strategic buyers. At approximately C$0.06 per share and using the April 2026 base count of 316.7M shares, implied market cap is roughly C$19M; factoring in post-April placements (potentially 390M+ shares), the implied market cap rises to approximately C$23M — still modest for a district-scale critical minerals project in a Tier-1 jurisdiction. Strategic acquisition interest in non-Chinese antimony development assets in OECD jurisdictions remains structurally elevated. Score of 2 is maintained: strategic conditions are favourable but the absence of a compliant resource prevents a quantified acquisition discount analysis.
analyst_summary: Churchill Resources (CRI.V) holds the Foxtrot past-producing antimony mine district in central Newfoundland and is advancing a multi-property, multi-commodity explorer position (Black Raven/Frost Cove, Golden Baie, Taylor Brook, Pomley Cove Pond, Taylors Room). STATUS as of August 30, 2026: Spring 2026 assay results were released yesterday (August 29, 2026), ending a 47-day post-completion silence. The Spring 2026 program totalled 23 drillholes and 4,267m at Pomley Cove Pond and Frost Cove North. Headline intercept: 19.23% Sb over 1.40m at Frost Cove North. A new copper-silver prospect returned 0.78% Cu with 6.12 g/t Ag over 6.22m, broadening the polymetallic thesis beyond antimony-gold. The 5,000m Taylor Brook drill program is underway with a $2,600,000 placement closed. Macro tailwind intact: China's antimony export controls remain in force; US DoD has awarded over USD $100M to Tier-1 jurisdiction antimony projects since late 2025. Cap table per April 2026 MD&A extraction (most recent reliable data): 316,681,940 shares issued, 342,756,940 fully diluted (2,625,000 warrants + 23,450,000 options — strike prices and expiry dates not extracted). Post-April 2026 placements (the $3M March placement at $0.08/share and the $2.6M Taylor Brook financing) likely push shares outstanding to approximately 390M+ — not captured in the extracted data. No NI 43-101 compliant resource on file; all resource/reserve fields are null. Maintain WATCH, confidence low: the resolved assay catalyst and the new Cu-Ag intercept improve the geological thesis, and the active Taylor Brook program is a genuine near-term catalyst; however, the absence of a compliant resource, heavy and growing share structure, and unconfirmed full scope of the Spring 2026 results limit conviction. Taylor Brook first-assay results are now the primary forward catalyst.
